 About the role 

 We are seeking a full-time/part-time Research Associate in Energy Demand Flexibility to join the EDOL research programme at the Department of Engineering Science in central Oxford. The post is funded by EPSRC and is fixed term to 31 Dec 2027.

 Energy Demand Observatory and Laboratory (EDOL) is collecting smart meter data from thousands of UK households to better understand energy consumption patterns and how these change over time. Oxford leads the EDOL Flexibility Lab, which conducts interventions to further understand behavioural and technical flexibility and their limits.

 You will be responsible for analysing these data to find evidence of flexibility and to devise new interventions and approaches to data collection. You will collaborate with researchers across the programme at University College London, University of Exeter and the School of Geography at the University of Oxford. 

 About you 

 You should possess good quantitative and data analytical skills, a good understanding of and interest in energy systems, and a willingness to try new approaches.

 How to apply 

 Applications for this vacancy are to be made online via our e-recruitment system and should include the covering letter/supporting statement (describing how you meet the criteria), a CV, and names of two academic references.

 The position is a full-time/part-time fixed term post available to 31 December 2027.

 The closing date for applications is 12.00 noon on Friday 18 December 2026. 

 Informal enquiries may be addressed to Prof Phil Grunewald  philipp.grunewald@eng.ox.ac.uk  

 Further information can be found at   https://eng.ox.ac.uk/jobs 

 Applications are particularly welcome from women and black and minority ethnic candidates who are under-represented in academic posts in Oxford. The Department is committed to equality and valuing diversity and holds an Athena Swan Bronze award, highlighting its commitment to promoting gender equality in academia. The University is a Living Wage Employer, holds an Athena Swan Silver Award, an HR Excellence in Research and a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award and is a Stonewall Diversity Champion. Our staff and students come from all over the world, and we seek to create a friendly and inclusive culture. Diversity is positively encouraged, through our EDI Committee, working groups and networks, for example   eng.ox.ac.uk/women-in-engineering , as well as a number of   family friendly policies .

Job Title: Research Fellow (Economics)
Job Reference:  609
Department: Economics
Contract Type: Fixed-Term Contract
Contract End Date: 13 November 2028
Hours: Full-Time (1.0 FTE)
Full-Time Salary Range: £36,320.00 to £46,970.00 per annum
Location: HMRC Datalab, 14 Westfield Avenue, London, E20 1HZ
About the Role

 

The Centre for the Analysis of Taxation (CenTax) is a research centre dedicated to advancing knowledge and understanding of taxation policies and practices. Led by Professor Arun Advani (Warwick) and Professor Andy Summers (LSE), research is undertaken to generate rigorous quantitative evidence on tax at the top, develop targeted and feasible reforms, and communicate findings transparently to policy, media and civil society stakeholders.  Projects include analysis of the characteristics, behaviours and impacts of high earners in the UK; analyses of the UK’s “non-dom” regime, top-end migration, capital gains, and evaluation of policies for taxing wealth in the UK. Further details are available on the CenTax webpage.

 

As a post-doctoral Research Fellow, you will undertake research contributing to and supporting the work of CenTax, using administrative tax data accessed via the UK tax authority’s secure research facility, HMRC Datalab. In particular, you will contribute to new research focused on the taxation of trusts. As well as direct responsibility for data analysis, you will help to supervise a team of research assistants, and contribute to designing, writing and presenting academic papers and policy reports. There is particular emphasis on career development, supported by exposure to a range of research tasks and mentoring from lead researchers.

 

As part of the CenTax team, you would benefit from our existing data access and infrastructure built up over many years of research. This is by far the most comprehensive access to UK tax data of any research team, including several datasets on trusts and offshore income/gains that have never previously been used for research purposes.

 

The post is initially until 13th September 2028 with the intention to extend the contract to September 2029, subject to funding.

 

Base Location: HMRC Datalab, 14 Westfield Avenue, London E20 1HZ. There is also access to CenTax’s office spaces in the London School of Economics. A London weighting of £5,000 per year will be provided.

About You

 

You will hold a good honours degree and a PhD in Economics (or be close to submission), ideally in the area of public economics, with a focus on offshore wealth and tax evasion/avoidance.

 

Any publication(s) or working papers in the area of offshore wealth and/or tax evasion and avoidance would be an advantage.

 

About the Department

 

The Department of Economics at the University of Warwick consistently ranks among the top economics departments in Europe and globally. In the 2021 Research Excellence Framework, which assesses the quality of research in UK higher education institutions, 99% of the Department’s research was rated world-leading or internationally excellent, placing us 2nd in the UK for Economics.

How to Apply

 

To apply, please click APPLY below and submit an application form by the closing deadline.

 

You will be asked to add your personal details and include two attachments:

 

CV
Cover Letter

 

These attachments should:

 

Outline employment and education history (including your most recent employment).
Demonstrate your skills, experience, and qualifications, and how you meet the essential and desirable criteria in the Job Description.
 

Please ensure your application clearly evidences the essential criteria, as the hiring panel may not be able to shortlist your application if these are not demonstrated.

 

Interviews will be held on a date to be confirmed.

Job Description

 

For more information about essential and desirable knowledge, skills, experience, and qualifications for this position, please refer to the Job Description (JD) by clicking the link below:

 

↪ JD - Research Fellow (Economics) (609)

PhD Status

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5.

 

Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow level, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6.

 

Benefits

 

At the University of Warwick, you will have access to a wide range of benefits.

 

an attractive pension scheme;
a leading annual leave allowance;
excellent learning and development opportunities;
savings and discounts on a wide range of products and services;
generous maternity, paternity, and adoption leave;
onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work-life balance and support flexible working where this is compatible with the requirements of the role. Click here to find out more.

 

We are proud to be a Living Wage Employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, our Relocation Guide provides information about working at the University of Warwick and what may be involved in the relocation process.

 

Culture

 

At the University of Warwick, committed to creating a community built on mutual respect and dignity, and a welcoming working and learning environment.

 

We recognise and value the visible and non-visible differences within our community. Wherever possible, we seek to go beyond our legal obligations by removing economic, social, and cultural barriers to creating an environment in which everyone has the opportunity to thrive and achieve their full potential.

 

We welcome and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and communities, regardless of age, disability, sex or gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion or belief, sexual or romantic orientation, culture or background. Click here to find out more about social inclusion at the University. 

 

We currently hold a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award, an Athena Swan Silver Award, and a Disability Smart Bronze Award. We are also one of the six founding institutions of the EUTOPIA European University Alliance. Click here to find out more about our awards and accreditations.

About the role

Applicants are invited to apply for one Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network Researcher position funded by Horizon Europe Marie Currie Doctoral Network grant of the Commission of European Council to develop novel AI/ML method for optimal data-driven vulnerability mapping for power distribution networks. The positions involve undertaking full time research in data-efficient visibility, optimal data selection/compression, vulnerability mapping, and physics-informed AI integration for power distribution networks.

What you would be doing

You will conduct research on optimal, data-driven vulnerability mapping for power distribution networks, with a focus on data-efficient system visibility, optimal data selection and compression, vulnerability assessment, and the integration of physics-informed AI.

What we are looking for

You must have a good master’s degree in electrical engineering, with Power and Control Engineering major or (or equivalent) for appointment at Research Assistant level and have previous experience in power engineering with emphasis on power distribution networks modelling, analysis and control.

The position requires the candidate meets the academic requirement to register for PhD at Imperial College London.

The candidate needs to spend a 3 months of secondment in the consortium partner’s site in Spain and a 3 months of secondment in the industrial associate partner in UK.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 38 days off a year)

Further information

The candidates with travel restriction to secondment hosting countries need not apply. The position has a flexible start date between 1st April 2027 to 30th September 2027.

The candidates will work at the control and power group of the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering. Control and Power group has about twenty full time academic staffs, thirty post-doctoral research staffs and more than 60 PhD students. The group is known for its world leading research in control and power engineering. The group has ten IEEE Fellows and four Royal Academy of Engineering Fellows.

The post is available from 01 Feb 2027 for a fixed period of 36 months. The post is based in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering at Imperial College London (South Kensington Campus).

The salary will be a fixed salary and the rate will be either £44,284 per annum if the researcher is not entitled to the family allowance, or £48,797 if they are entitled to the family allowance.

If you require any further details on the role please contact: Prof. Bikash Pal b.pal@imperial.ac.uk.

Further information about the post is available in the job description.

Closing date: midnight on 3rd January 2027

 Overview 

 We are seeking a Research Fellow to join LungSight, a multidisciplinary project developing low-cost, non-invasive audio-visual AI for earlier identification of chronic lung disease. The project aims to support a shift from reactive, clinic-based diagnosis towards proactive home screening using everyday devices such as smartphones, tablets and home computers.

Based in the School of Engineering at the University of Southampton, you will lead the research engineering clinically informed acoustic features for fine-tuning machine learning models of respiratory health. You will work with large-scale real-world recordings of speech, breathing and cough, developing acoustic features that are robust to noise, demographic variation and different recording environments, predictive of early-stage chronic respiratory conditions and explainable in terms of the natural history of disease. You will also contribute to development of machine learning models and to the integration of audio with visual and clinical information.

LungSight is a multi-university collaboration also involving Manchester Metropolitan University, the University of Cambridge, the University of Leicester, the University of Leeds, and the University of Sheffield alongside NHS and third-sector partners. This post will work particularly closely with a complementary PDRA at the University of Sheffield, whose research will focus more strongly on development of machine learning models while the Southampton post has a stronger focus on acoustic features and clinical knowledge mapping. The role offers opportunities for high-quality publications, open research outputs, clinical and stakeholder engagement, and career development at the interface of AI and healthcare.

 Main duties and responsibilities 

 Develop and evaluate acoustic feature sets predictive of respiratory health using speech, breathing and cough recordings.

 Curate, pre-process and analyse large-scale real-world audio datasets, including sensitive healthcare and helpline recordings processed within appropriate secure data environments.

 Fine-tune and validate models on labelled respiratory datasets and clinically relevant downstream tasks, assessing accuracy, generalisability and clinical utility.

 Investigate potential confounding factors, demographic bias, background-noise effects and effects of recording environment, to support feature robustness and equitable model performance.

 Contribute to development of self-supervised models, working closely with the Sheffield PDRA who will lead complementary machine learning research; investigate how engineered physiological features can be combined with learned representations from the Sheffield machine-learning work.

 Collaborate with project researchers to develop multimodal approaches combining acoustic, visual and clinical information for respiratory disease screening.

 Work closely with researchers across the LungSight consortium, including Manchester Metropolitan Sheffield, Cambridge, Leicester and Leeds Universities, as well as clinical, NHS, patient/public and third-sector partners; participate in project meetings, joint research activities and dissemination.

 Lead and contribute to high-quality research publications and presentations, support project reporting, and contribute to the supervision and development of students where appropriate.

 You should hold a PhD (or equivalent research experience) in Computer Science, Electronic Engineering, Speech/Audio Processing, Machine Learning, Biomedical Engineering or a closely related discipline, with research experience in speech, audio, acoustic signal processing or closely related time-series analysis.

 About this role  

 The research associate will join the Interface and Electronic Materials Laboratory at the Oxford Materials Department for a project, under the leadership of Prof Sebastian Bonilla.

 They will be playing an active role in the project research activities and contribute to the overall team’s aim of understanding and developing improved solar cells. In this project, they will be responsible for investigating, developing, and optimising nanolayer dielectrics that can serve as selective, passivating, and interconnecting contacts enabling perovskite-on-silicon tandem solar cells.

 The project will be carried out in close collaboration with Prof Henry Snaith’s ‘Photovoltaic and Optoelectronic Device Group’.

 In addition to the fundamental work required to develop highly efficient nanolayer interconnects, they will develop the cell production processes in collaboration with a team of doctoral students, postdocs, and academics at the Department of Physics, University of Oxford.

 They will use solar cell processing and characterisation techniques, including dielectric thin film synthesis via oxidation, PVD, CVD, and ALD, making use the National Thin Film Cluster Deposition Facility for Advanced Functional Materials. Electrical, optical and morphological characterisation will be conducted using techniques such as photoconductance, PL, EL, EQE, SunsVoc, standardised IV, reflectance spectrometry, SEM, AFM, and EBIC.

 This project will involve working with external commercial and academic partners, requiring excellent communication and organisational skills.

 The role will also include publishing and disseminating scientific results through journal articles and conference presentations, and developing new grant proposals for future work.

 Responsibilities will also include involvement with other projects in the research group in terms of supervision and mentoring of junior students, and support for developing new research topics within the research team’s fields of expertise.

 About you 

 With a relevant PhD (or close to obtaining one), together with relevant experience in the field of solar cells you will be self-motivated, able to plan and deliver a research project, and have a strong publication record.

 Ideally, you will have experience in semiconductor clean rooms, processing, and electrical and optical characterisation of semiconductor devices. 

 Benefits 

 38 days holidays including Bank Holidays, subsidised travel scheme, excellent pension scheme, comprehensive childcare service, flexible working.

 How to Apply 

 All applications must be made online using the Oxford University E-Recruitment system, no later than 12 noon on 1 December 2026 . You will be required to upload a CV and a 3-page Supporting Statement as part of your application.  Please do not attach any manuscripts, papers, transcripts, mark sheets or certificates as these will not be considered as part of your application. 

 Only applications received online by 12.00 midday BST on   Tue 1 December 2026 can be considered. 

 Interviews are scheduled to take place at the Department of Materials (interview date to be confirmed) and you must be available, either by Teams/Zoom or in person.

 Please note in normal circumstances only interview travel expenses within the UK will be reimbursed. 

 Please do let us know if you require any more information. Many thanks for your assistance in advance.

A position exists for a Research Assistant/Associate in Power Electronics Packaging and Integration in the Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge, working with Professor Teng Long's Power Electronics Research Group in West Cambridge, UK.

The post holder will design and validate advanced chip-scale and module-level packages for SiC and GaN devices, including die attachment, interconnections, thermal interfaces and heat-spreading structures. Research will combine electrical, thermal and thermomechanical modelling with power semiconductor electrical and thermal testing. Duties include finite-element and compact thermal-network modelling, parameter extraction, transient thermal impedance measurements, structure-function analysis and junction-to-case thermal resistance assessment. Experimental results will validate models and guide improvements in package design. Power cycling and failure analysis will link package degradation to measured changes in device behaviour. The post holder will develop automated testing and analysis methods, publish findings, collaborate with academic and industrial partners, and contribute to student supervision and research proposals.

Applicants must have, or be close to obtaining, a PhD in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline, with research in power electronics packaging, integration or thermal management. Knowledge of power semiconductor packaging, interconnections, thermal management and reliability is essential, together with at least two accepted or published journal papers. Experience in multiphysics or thermal-network modelling, semiconductor testing, transient thermal characterisation, or test automation and data analysis using MATLAB, Python or equivalent tools is desirable.

Appointment at Research Associate level is dependent on having a PhD. Those who have submitted but not yet received their PhD will be appointed at Research Assistant level, which will be amended to Research Associate once the PhD has been awarded.

The post is full-time and funded for 12 months or until 31 December 2027, whichever comes sooner.

The Role

 

This is an exciting opportunity for an early career Research Associate to join Newcastle University’s Population Health Sciences Institute in a three year post. You will be working with and mentored by Dr. Eugene Tang  as part of his NIHR Advanced Fellowship, to support this mixed-methods work. It is anticipated that this role will provide an excellent platform for you to be mentored and receive support from an experienced academic General Practitioner with the aim of developing your research interests, experiences and skills in the areas of stroke and dementia

 

The ideal candidate would be an early career health services researcher who has a PhD by the time of role start in a healthcare related area. You should have experience and interest in both quantitative and qualitative research techniques. A NIHR Advanced Fellowship is funding this fixed term post for 31 months (1.0 WTE). You will be working on the project “Identification and Reducing the Impact of those at Risk of Dementia for All Stroke Survivors in the Community”. You will support the work on a mixed-methods research programme, which includes risk prediction modelling using advanced statistical techniques including machine learning, qualitative interviews and co-production workshops. There will also be opportunities to develop your own area of interest including support for a career development award as part of this role.

 

You will be based in the Henry Wellcome Building as part of the stroke research group. You will also be part of the Academic Primary and Community Care Unit (APCCU), which is a virtual unit which aims to bring together leading experts within primary and community care systems to build capacity in academic primary and community care within the region.

 

You will need to supply a CV and a cover letter outlining how you are suitable for the role.

About the role

We are seeking a Pathology Research Technician to join the Faculty of Medicine’s Research Pathology Facility, based at Charing Cross Campus. You will provide high-quality histological support to a range of research projects, working alongside researchers and scientists to deliver specialist pathology services, including immunohistochemistry, tissue processing and multiplex immunofluorescence.

What you would be doing

You will provide support for a range of translational research projects across the Faculty of Medicine, with a particular focus on projects within the Department of Surgery and Cancer. Your responsibilities will include:

Providing a high-quality histological service to support research projects and biomarker studies.
Processing research tissue samples, including fixation, embedding, preparation of paraffin blocks and sectioning of FFPE and frozen tissue samples.
Optimising and validating antibodies for immunostaining, developing and establishing standard operating procedures, and performing routine stains such as H&E and Ki67.
Performing multiplex immunofluorescence using the COMET Lunaphore system and contributing to the development of new techniques, e.g. RNAscope.
Preparing tissue sections for specialist applications, including spatial transcriptomics, and constructing, sectioning and staining tissue microarrays.
Scanning and analysing stained slides, archiving images and supporting the annotation of tissue sections and scoring of biomarker staining in collaboration with pathologists.
Maintaining accurate laboratory records and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations, including Human Tissue Authority (HTA) requirements and Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP) standards.
Managing the storage and tracking of histological specimens in accordance with Tissue Bank protocols.
Supporting the day-to-day running of the facility, including ordering consumables, maintaining equipment and ensuring an efficient working laboratory.
Providing advice, training and technical assistance to investigators and students, while contributing to laboratory meetings, grant reports and scientific publications.
Working collaboratively with colleagues across Imperial, including travelling to other campuses where necessary to access specialist equipment and services.

 

What we are looking for

Educated to Master's level, or equivalent experience, in a biological discipline.
Proven research experience in a technical or scientific role, with practical experience in histological processing of tissue samples.
Experience optimising and validating antibodies for immunostaining and constructing and analysing tissue microarrays.
Good working knowledge of microscopy, cell biology and pathology, including the ability to recognise tumour tissue.
Knowledge of the ethical and regulatory requirements surrounding tissue and biofluid storage and use, including the Human Tissue Act.
Experience with biochemical assays and/or in vitro cancer studies.
Well-developed analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to analyse and present data using relevant software.
Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to maintain accurate laboratory records and an efficient, well-organised laboratory.
Able to work accurately under pressure, manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively as part of a team, providing training and assistance to others where needed.
Experience ordering laboratory consumables and maintaining equipment.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to use science for humanity.
Benefit from a sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days’ annual leave and generous pension schemes).
Access to a range of workplace benefits including a flexible working policy from day one, generous family leave packages, on-site leisure facilities and cycle-to-work scheme.
Interest-free season ticket loan schemes for travel.
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week).

This role is for a fixed-term contract for 20 months in the first instance.

If you require any further details about the role, please contact Professor Robert Goldin – r.goldin@imperial.ac.uk

About the Faculty

The Faculty of Science and Engineering at Manchester Metropolitan University delivers internationally recognised research and innovation across computing, mathematics, engineering and data-driven technologies. The Faculty is committed to addressing societal challenges through interdisciplinary research, impact, knowledge exchange and partnerships with industry, government and communities.

About the Department

The School of Computing and Mathematics has a strong reputation for research and innovation in artificial intelligence, responsible AI, data science and digital technologies. This role will contribute to the School's REF2029 impact development activities, supporting nationally and internationally recognised work on responsible AI governance, public participation in AI, and evidence-based policy development. The team operates a flexible hybrid working pattern with opportunities for on-campus and stakeholder-facing engagement activities.

About the Project
This 12-month fixed-term post will support the impact case study “Building Trust in AI: From Marginalised Communities to Cross-Government Policy and Guidance”. The project draws on a portfolio of responsible AI initiatives including the People's Panel for AI, the People's Charter for AI, government AI governance activities, SME engagement programmes and regional AI policy development. Working closely with Professor Keeley Crockett, the research manager and collaborators, the postholder will gather and evaluate evidence of impact, support stakeholder engagement, and help develop outputs for REF2029, academic publications, policy briefings and reports.

About the Role & Team
You will join an active responsible AI research team and work with academic researchers, local government, policymakers, industry partners, community organisations and SMEs. Day-to-day activities will include qualitative and quantitative research, data collection and analysis, stakeholder interviews, impact evaluation, workshop support, evidence collection and report writing. You will contribute to the development of impact case studies, policy outputs and publications while helping coordinate engagement activities across local, national and international stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Collect, analyse and report qualitative and quantitative impact evidence.
Evaluate adoption and influence of AI governance frameworks, including the UK Government AI Playbook.
Conduct interviews, surveys, workshops and stakeholder engagement activities.
Maintain auditable REF2029 impact evidence and stakeholder testimonials.
Support delivery of the People's Charter for AI, People's Panel for AI and Responsible AI SME Charter activities.
Contribute academic papers, policy briefings, reports and impact case study narratives.

Key Skills & Experience

Research experience in participatory AI and responsible AI.
Experience collecting and analysing qualitative and quantitative data.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Ability to communicate findings to diverse audiences and stakeholders.
Knowledge and experience of public engagement, impact and knowledge exchange activities.
Experience with research software such as NVivo and standard data analysis tools.
Doctoral qualification, or working towards one, in AI or a related discipline.

 The Department of Geography and Environmental Science at the University of Reading seeks a Postdoctoral Research Associate to join LAMDA (Land–atmosphere interactions as a mechanism of dryland formation), a project funded by a European Research Council (ERC) Starting Grant and led by Dr Akash Koppa. LAMDA will develop a new theory of how humid regions turn into drylands. Specifically, it will combine paleoclimatic reconstructions with Earth system, ecosystem demographics, and atmospheric transport models to trace how drylands, vegetation, and land–atmosphere fluxes have co-evolved since 850 CE. 

 You will lead research in one or more of three directions: (a) constraining Earth system model simulations of the last millennium with paleoclimatic proxy records through data assimilation, (b) quantifying how the function, structure, and demography of vegetation respond to long-term drying and feed back to the atmosphere, and (c) assessing how human modification of the land surface, such as deforestation, afforestation, and irrigation, changes the rate at which drylands form. You will run model simulations on high-performance computing facilities, publish as lead author, and help supervise PhD students in the group. The post also offers close collaboration with research groups at the University of Bern and Ghent University, including extended research stays. 

 Reading is a leading centre for weather, climate, and environmental science, and ECMWF will move onto the Whiteknights campus in 2027. You will receive support to develop your own fellowship and grant applications.

 A PhD (or near completion) in atmospheric science, climate science, Earth system science, ecology, hydrology, physical geography, physics, or a closely related field

Location

As part of our recruitment approach, internal candidates will receive priority consideration at the shortlisting stage.

About the role

As a Research Fellow in Laboratory Systems Biology Cancer Research you will lead the delivery of cutting-edge interdisciplinary research project that combines computational systems biology and laboratory science to better treat cancers.  

This role builds on breakthrough results showing that computational models can predict how lymphoma patients respond to therapy, and expands these approaches to multiple cancers. This project will focus on experimentally developing biomarkers that will enable systems biology models to predict response to therapy in the clinic. You will lead the delivery of this 2-year Future Leaders Fellowship-funded project, produce high quality academic publications, and share your work nationally and internationally at academic conferences. The flexible nature of the funding enables you to shape the project direction, and pursue the most promising results. 

You will also benefit from substantial mentorship, training opportunities, and exposure to a variety of experimental and computational techniques that will contribute to your own development towards research and innovation leadership.

About you

You will hold, or be near completion of a PhD in molecular biology, cancer biology, systems biology, cell biology, bioinformatics, or closely related fields. You will have experience generating scientific wet-lab data, presenting the data in figures, and presenting the results in peer reviewed manuscripts and presentations. You will have the ability to quickly learn new experimental and computational techniques to adapt to new research directions. 

You will conduct high quality independent research to shape the direction of the project and independently manage your workload and time. You will have the ability to plan experiments, and conduct some computational work in parallel, enabling the iteration of experimental and computational insight. 

You will have the ability to quickly learn detailed molecular signalling pathways, how molecular signalling impacts cancer cell fates, and how altered cell fates may impact patient responses to treatment and outcomes. You will have molecular biology and cell culture expertise to enable you to test model predictions. You will ideally have some experience with computer code and the ability to pick up new computational approaches to perform simulations designed to address these questions. 

You will be able to communicate effectively with the research group, and collaborate closely with a growing interdisciplinary blood cancer research team at BSMS. This includes communicating clearly with laboratory scientists, computational scientists, and non-scientific stakeholders. You will be embedded within Sussex Blood Cancer Research, a growing research group that combines blood cancer researchers across the University of Sussex and BSMS. You will benefit from the Sussex Cancer Research Centre, which unites cancer reseachers at the University of Sussex, University of Brighton, BSMS, and multiple NHS trusts across Sussex (www.sussexcancer.org). 

About our School

Brighton and Sussex Medical School (BSMS) is an equal partnership between the Universities of Sussex and Brighton together with NHS organisations throughout the South-East Region. BSMS is committed to inclusivity, sustainability, medical education in a multi-professional context, and promoting the highest possible standards in our teaching, clinical practice and research (ranging from early translational to applied). 

Working together, our Academics, Technicians and Professional Services staff co-ordinate the passionate delivery of teaching and research, allowing us to remain one of the leading choices of medical schools in the UK. Our staff are multiskilled and work across varied teams, which are diverse, experienced and dedicated.  

Our object as a School is to strive for excellence in education, training and research allowing us to support all in a constantly changing healthcare sector. We work to create a nurturing and supportive environment in which our staff and our students can succeed and thrive. 

Our medical research has developed a strong reputation for making a real impact locally, nationally and internationally. 

Ultimately, our research aims to: 

•improve medical treatment 

•answer fundamental biomedical and clinical questions 

•deliver more personalised healthcare to patients. 

Please find further information regarding the School at Brighton and Sussex Medical School
 
Brighton and Sussex Medical School is proud to hold a Gold Athena Swan Award. 

Why work here

Our university is situated off the A27, next to the beautiful South Downs where you will enjoy everything that our 150-acre campus has to offer. We are accessible by public transport; Falmer train station is a five-minute walk to campus and several bus stops are located within campus. We also have dedicated cycling paths and encourage our staff to use these with our offering of a cycle to work scheme.  

Sussex is a renowned, multi-accredited, research-led International University and this is only possible because of the people that work here. Whether you are a member of Faculty, part of a Professional Services team or a Student, it’s our people that make us great and we want you to be part of that.  

Find out more about our reward and benefits package.  

Find out about our equality, diversity and inclusion  

Further Key Information 

Please contact Simon Mitchell (S.A.Mitchell@bsms.ac.uk) for informal enquiries. 

Please include links to any papers or preprints you have produced, or pre-publication manuscripts if appropriate. 

For full details and how to apply see our vacancies page. 

The University is committed to equality and valuing diversity, and applications are particularly welcomed from women and black and minority ethnic candidates, who are under-represented in academic posts in Science, Technology, Engineering, Medicine and Mathematics (STEMM) at Sussex.  

Please note that this position may be subject to ATAS clearance if you require visa sponsorship.  

See more vacancies at the University of Brighton 

The University of Sussex values the diversity of its staff and students, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

About the role

We are looking to recruit a Research Assistant to work on an exciting study investigating Disorders of Consciousness (DoC). In people with DoC, this study will investigate the effects of intravenous DMT administration on measures of neural complexity, neuroplasticity, and awareness.

The study, funded by the Medical Research Council (MRC), is entitled “N,N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT) for Disorders of Consciousness (DoC)” (DMT-DoC). You will primarily be working on the DMT-DoC study. This placebo-controlled study involves administering intravenous DMT and a saline placebo to patients with DoC. We will record electroencephalography (EEG) alongside other physiological and behavioural measures before, during, and after drug/placebo administration.

You will work in the Computational Neurology group of academic neurologist neurologist Dr Gregory Scott, within the Department of Brain Sciences, with a team of collaborators including experts in clinical neurology, psychedelics, neuropsychopharmacology, DoC, EEG, computer science, and neurophysiology.

This is an exciting opportunity to work on a study that could pave the way to a new class of treatment for DoC and improve our understanding of the neural mechanisms of consciousness.

What you would be doing

Your main responsibilities will be to conduct the essential day-to-day running of the study, support the rest of the study team in regulatory and ethical approval, participant recruitment, and the arranging and conduct of study visits, help with data collection and handling, assist with the preparation and maintenance of study-related documentation and associated administrative duties, and undertake data management and data analysis activities as required. You will also support the writing of research papers and reports, submission of papers to refereed journals, presentation of the research, coordination of patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) and study monitoring activities, and attracting further research funding to the group. You will also actively participate more broadly in the research programme of the group.

What we are looking for

You should have a First/Masters degree (or equivalent) in Neuroscience, Psychology or related discipline. You should have experience of working in a research environment and knowledge of neurological disorders and brain injury. Experience of analysing EEG and neuroimaging data, as well as experience of arranging patient interactions, is desirable but not essential.

A unique opportunity to work on an exciting experimental study
Progress your research career with support from academic neurologist Dr Scott and the study team, in a department with an excellent track record in supporting early career researchers and clinical academics

Research Associate - Dyspraxia Research - (9560)

About the University and Institute

Manchester Metropolitan University is committed to delivering Excellent Education and Excellent Research with Impact as part of our ambitious Road to 2030 strategy. We are proud of our inclusive and collaborative academic community, where our people make a positive difference through education, research, professional practice and engagement.

The Institute of Sport at Manchester Metropolitan University combines expertise from across the University to deliver research, innovation and partnerships that improve health, sport and human performance. Working across all four Faculties, the Institute develops ambitious projects that strengthen research capability, build meaningful partnerships with business and the sporting sector, and deliver real-world impact. From creating new research and innovation centres to developing strategic partnerships and delivering high-profile national and international events, our work is varied, collaborative and forward-thinking.

About the Schools 

This post is based in the School of Sport and Exercise Sciences, one of the UK's biggest and most popular sports and exercise schools, in a city that's alive with sport. Sport science is a powerful discipline with a wide-ranging impact. You could push an exceptional athlete to elite standards, performing at the highest levels. Or, you could support a cardiac patient through their rehabilitation, improving their quality of life. With the right skills, you can make a profound difference to both individuals and communities.

This post is also aligned to research in the School of Psychology, home to a hub of experts, committed to understanding the challenges of today to improve the futures of individuals and communities. Staff are accredited specialists and psychologists at the forefront of current practice both in the UK and internationally, implementing their expertise to inform teaching and research.

The School of Psychology houses a range of state-of-the-art facilities, including our Neurocognitive Laboratories which feature a brain stimulation lab and virtual reality (VR) equipment. We are proud of our successful history of working in partnership with students on our courses, preparing them both academically and professionally for their future careers in psychology.

Our dyspraxia research has had a global impact, focusing on children's health and learning. You will join a large team of researchers working in movement science and with a focus on young children with dyspraxia, their families, and the educational and clinical networks surrounding them. 

About the Project  

Two decades of interdisciplinary motor-learning research at Manchester Metropolitan University have transformed rehabilitation for children with Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD/ dyspraxia) by translating cognitive neuroscience into routine NHS practice. Through co-production with clinicians and families, we developed Watch Me Do It, a free, multilingual, first-person video resource website. It is now embedded across 41 NHS Foundation Trusts' occupational therapy services, adopted by international advocacy groups, public-health networks and users across 92 countries. The toolkit has transformed professional practice by replacing fragmented written advice with standardised, research-evidenced visual modelling, increasing clinician efficiency and user confidence, improving children's functional independence, strengthening parental capacity, extending therapy provision during waiting periods, and advancing equitable access to evidence-based care.

About the Team, Role, and Responsibilities

The successful candidate will be line managed by Professor Paul Holmes, one of the members of the Dyspraxia research team. In addition, researchers Dr Dave Wright, Dr Greg Wood, and Impact Manager, Vera Baron will provide project guidance and support.

You will work with the team to capture all aspects of impact relating to the Watch Me Do It resource. Specifically, you will:

Collect and report testimonials from children and parents who have used the Watch Me Do It resource
Collect and report testimonials from occupational therapists who have used the Watch Me Do It resource
Collect and report testimonials from SENCOs/school-teachers who use the Watch Me Do It resource
Identify and quantify time savings and cost savings for occupational therapists using the Watch Me Do It resource
Identify and quantify meaningful outcomes from Watch Me Do It use across all communities using the resource
Conduct outreach with schools to widen adoption and reach (e.g., inclusion in SEND provision)
Support the University team with dissemination of findings at academic and professional conferences
Assist with data collection for a new multiple baseline study with the Watch Me Do It resource
Promote the Watch Me Do It resource across Europe and with global partners

To learn more about role and requirements, please read the Job Description provided below.  

If you would like to join our people and share our ambition, we would love to hear from you! 

Application & Assessment 

To apply, please submit a CV and covering letter detailing your suitability, on the application portal. Please be aware that only applications including a cover letter may be considered at shortlisting stage. 
Assessment will include a competency-based interview and are expected to be held on 14th or 15th of December.
Due to the volume of applications, we receive, we sometimes close our vacancies early. It is therefore advisable to apply as early as possible if you would like to be considered for a role. 
For informal enquiries, about this vacancy, please contact Professor Paul Holmes (s.holmes@mmu.ac.uk) or Dr David Wright (d.j.wright@mmu.ac.uk).

We believe in working together, sharing knowledge and valuing everyone's contributions. Develop your skills, further your knowledge and be part of a team who are transforming lives, every single day! 

Further Information

Manchester Metropolitan University fosters an inclusive culture of belonging that promotes equity and celebrates diversity. We value a diverse workforce for the innovation and diversity of thought it brings and welcome applications from local and international communities, including those from Black, Asian, and Minority Ethnic backgrounds, disabled people, and LGBTQ+ individuals. 

We support a range of flexible working arrangements, including hybrid and tailored schedules, which can be discussed with your line manager. If you require reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process or in your role, please let us know so we can provide appropriate support.

A post-doctoral position is available to take a leading research role in an industry-facing HBLB funded research project entitled “Toward Racehorse Injury Prevention: A Computer Vision-Based Approach for Monitoring Behaviour in Stabled Racehorses and Early Identification of Musculoskeletal Injuries”, a project to be conducted in collaboration with Vet Vision AI and Johnston Racing.

The project uses computer vision and artificial intelligence to identify behavioural indicators of musculoskeletal injury — primarily limb injuries — in stabled racehorses. Continuous monitoring of behaviour in the stabled environment offers a unique opportunity to capture rich behavioural data to validate a computer vision tool measuring 24-hour time budgets and behavioural patterns, with the goal of developing alerts that flag injury risk during the training season. Vet Vision AI has developed this technology to characterise behaviour in healthy horses and to detect patterns associated with disease in hospitalised horses. This project applies these techniques to racehorse injury monitoring and prevention for the first time. 

Identifying behavioural patterns that precede injury would be a step-change for equine health, welfare and performance. It would open a new area of research into racehorse behaviour and underpin early-warning systems with the potential to change how the industry monitors and protects horses in training.

This is a senior postdoctoral role that demands deep expertise in equine behaviour and veterinary science, strong industry credibility, and the judgement to lead delivery across academic and commercial partners. The successful applicant will join a collaborative and well-connected research group within the School of Veterinary Medicine and Science (SVMS). The post is primarily research-focused, with some teaching and administrative duties. The role involves significant time working directly with racehorses through the project partner Johnston Racing, and close collaboration with industry partner Vet Vision AI.   

The postholder will collaborate widely across SVMS research teams and contribute to mentoring undergraduate and postgraduate researchers. SVMS was ranked second in the UK for research power in the most recent Research Excellence Framework and has consistently ranked first in the National Student Survey since 2011. The post is based at Sutton Bonington Campus and will involve independent travel to project partners Vet Vision AI (Derbyshire) and Johnston Racing (North Yorkshire). This is a three-year, full-time (36.25 weekly hours) post offered at an enhanced salary reflecting the seniority of the role.

 The University of Oxford is a stimulating work environment, which enjoys an international reputation as a world-class centre of excellence. Our research plays a key role in tackling many global challenges, from reducing our carbon emissions to developing vaccines during a pandemic. Oxford Physics is one of the largest and most eminent departments in Europe, pursuing forefront research alongside training the next generation of leaders in Physics. The successful candidate will be based in the Condensed Matter Physics Sub-department at the Clarendon Laboratory, Oxford. We are seeking a Postdoctoral Research Associate to work on an exciting new project entitled “Conjugated Spacers for Tuneable 2D Perovskites (TUNE-2D)”, funded jointly by EPSRC in the UK and DFG in Germany.

 About the Role 

 Applications are invited for a Postdoctoral Research Associate to work on an exciting new project entitled “Conjugated Spacers for Tuneable 2D Perovskites (TUNE-2D)”, funded jointly between EPSRC in the UK and DFG in Germany. The project will investigate two-dimensional metal halide perovskites incorporating π-conjugated organic spacer molecules, with the aim of establishing quantitative correlations between spacer structure and material properties. The post will be based in the Condensed Matter Physics Sub-department and will report to Professor Laura Herz. The successful candidate will conduct the spectroscopic programme associated with the project, including ultrafast THz, absorption and photoluminescence measurements, as well as using cryogenic systems for temperature control. They will undertake research activities, adapt existing and develop new scientific techniques and experimental protocols, test hypotheses and analyse scientific data, and contribute ideas for new research directions. The postholder will manage their own academic research and administrative activities, collaborate with other group members and external collaborators in preparing scientific reports and journal articles, and present research results at national and international conferences and meetings. They will use specialist scientific equipment in a laboratory environment, including Class 4 lasers and thin-film semiconductor processing equipment, while observing laboratory safety protocols. This is a full-time, on-site position, fixed-term for three years, with a required start date of 1 March 2027.

 About You 

 Applicants should possess, or be close to obtaining, a PhD in physics, materials science or physical chemistry. They should have knowledge of semiconductor physics and a track record of working with next-generation novel materials for light-harvesting. You will have demonstrated expertise in a variety of advanced and ultrafast optical spectroscopic characterisation techniques, including time-resolved photoluminescence, absorption and photoconductivity, together with the related analysis and modelling. Experience with metal halide semiconductors would be desirable. You will have a good track record of high-quality publications and excellent verbal and written communication skills in English. You should be highly motivated, with excellent skills in working collaboratively and constructively as part of a team, as well as the ability to direct your own research and interpret your results independently.

 Are you naturally curious, analytical and motivated by making a difference? Do you enjoy uncovering insights, connecting information and helping organisations build meaningful relationships? If so, this could be the perfect opportunity to develop your prospect research career at one of the UK's leading universities.

 We’re hiring a Prospect Researcher to join our Campaigns and Alumni Relations (CAR) department. And you’ll be joining at an exciting time. As we approach the final stages of our ambitious fundraising campaign, your work will help shape what's next and ensure we're making the most of opportunities to engage our community.

 As part of the team you’ll be working in a department that helps build relationships with more than 330,000 alumni worldwide.

 Working closely with major gift fundraisers, you'll help identify and engage potential supporters whose philanthropy can transform opportunities for students, advance world-leading research and support projects that make a real difference locally and globally.

 This is a role where your research has a purpose. You'll help colleagues understand the interests, backgrounds and potential of alumni, donors and supporters, providing insights that inform conversations and strengthen relationships. You'll also help manage the pipeline of potential supporters, ensuring fundraisers can focus their time where it will have the greatest impact.

 Your work could include:

 Identifying alumni, donors and friends of the University with the capacity and inclination to support strategic priorities.

 Producing high-quality prospect briefings and background research for meetings, events and fundraising activity.

 Analysing wealth, biographical and philanthropic information from a range of sources to assess philanthropic potential.

 Managing prospect pipelines and helping ensure fundraising opportunities are progressed effectively.

 Supporting fundraising events by researching attendees and helping colleagues prepare for meaningful conversations.

 Working with colleagues across the University to uncover new engagement and fundraising opportunities.

 We're looking for someone who will:

 Thrive on applying their research to better engage people for our cause and bring us together to achieve more.

 Have a knack for spotting connections and opportunities.

 Be skilled at locating and linking relevant data from a variety of sources into user-friendly briefings.

 Be able to effectively communicate with non-data specialists and colleagues at all levels of seniority within the organisation.

 Have excellent organisational and time management skills.

The University’s Total Reward Package includes a competitive salary, a generous Pension Scheme and annual leave entitlement, as well as access to a range of learning and development courses to support your personal and professional development.

 We build teams of people from different heritages and lifestyles from across the world, whose talent and contributions complement each other to greatest effect. We believe diversity in all its forms delivers greater impact through research, teaching and student experience.

 The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

 We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more.

Research Assistant - EMBRACE Network Ref: 44414 (Part Time, Fixed Term)
Location
Brighton, UK
Hours
Part time considered up to a maximum of 0.8FTE / 29 hours per week. Requests for flexible working options will be considered (subject to business need). This post offers flexible-working, however, the employee is expected to work in-person at the Trafford Centre for at least 2-days per week.

Contract Type
Fixed Term Contract
As part of our recruitment approach, internal candidates will receive priority consideration at the shortlisting stage.

About the role

As a Research Assistant on the EMBRACE project (Equitable Midlife Brain Research Across Communities and Environments), you will play a key role in supporting an exciting international research initiative exploring how cognitive health can be assessed more equitably across diverse populations. 

Based within the Centre for Dementia Studies at the Brighton & Sussex Medical School, you will work closely with the Principal Investigator (Dr Claire Lancaster) and an interdisciplinary, international team of researchers, collaborators, community partners and digital technology specialists.

You will contribute to the coordination and delivery of project activities, including network meetings, narrative literature reviews, and co-design workshops with lived experience representatives (e.g., women experiencing menopause from minoritised ethnic groups, isolated coastal and rural communities). You will support the collection, management and analysis of qualitative and quantitative data, including thematic analysis of workshop transcripts, helping to synthesise insights from diverse communities and inform the development of an inclusive cognitive assessment framework. 

You will also contribute to the preparation of research outputs, dissemination activities and plans for future collaborative research. This is an excellent opportunity to develop your research skills and networks while contributing to innovative, collaborative research with the potential to advance equity and inclusion in cognitive health research.

About you

Ideally, you will have an undergraduate degree in Psychology or a related discipline, alongside experience or demonstrable skills in research and project coordination. You will be highly organised, able to manage competing priorities and deadlines, and confident communicating clearly with a range of audiences, including researchers, community partners and members of the public.

You will have experience of research ethics regulatory approvals, reviewing scientific literature, conducting interviews and/or focus groups, and undertaking qualitative data analysis, particularly thematic analysis. Strong organisational and time-management skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team are essential.

We would particularly welcome applicants with experience in scientific outreach, public engagement or public involvement in research. Knowledge of dementia and/or cognitive ageing would be an advantage, as would experience of research data management. 

Above all, you will be motivated to contribute to inclusive, collaborative research and interested in ensuring that diverse communities and perspectives are represented in the development of more equitable approaches to cognitive health assessment.

About our School

We are a diverse, collaborative research community with expertise in a wide variety of research areas, from laboratory research through to social science and clinical studies. Our close integration collaborations with local NHS organizations allows our researchers to work directly with the local population, improving their health while developing research work that can be applied nationally and globally. 

Here, at our School, our medical research has and continues to develop a strong reputation for making a real impact locally, nationally and internationally. Ultimately, our research aims to:

improve medical diagnosis and treatment 
answer fundamental biomedical and clinical questions
deliver more personalised healthcare to patients.
 

We are passionate about training and supporting our researchers at all levels, delivering research that is relevant to our stakeholders, accelerate its recognition and foster adoption of our findings to catalyse new research impact.

Please find further information regarding the School at Brighton and Sussex Medical School
 
Brighton and Sussex Medical School is proud to hold a Gold Athena Swan Award.

Why work here

Our university is situated off the A27, next to the beautiful South Downs where you will enjoy everything that our 150-acre campus has to offer. We are accessible by public transport; Falmer train station is a five-minute walk to campus and several bus stops are located within campus. We also have dedicated cycling paths and encourage our staff to use these with our offering of a cycle to work scheme.  

Sussex is a renowned, multi-accredited, research-led International University and this is only possible because of the people that work here. Whether you are a member of Faculty, part of a Professional Services team or a Student, it’s our people that make us great and we want you to be part of that. 

Find out more about our reward and benefits package. 

Find out about our equality, diversity and inclusion. 

Further Key Information 

Please contact Claire Lancaster Claire.Lancaster@sussex.ac.uk for informal enquiries.

The University of Sussex values the diversity of its staff and students, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Eligibility for sponsorship will depend on whether the candidate holds an existing Skilled Worker sponsorship which began before 4 April 2024, the salary offered, and/or whether a candidate can make use of tradeable points to meet the salary offered.

 UCL Mechanical Engineering has pioneered engineering education for over 165 years. The Department�s Orthopaedic Engineering group researches engineering, imaging and orthopaedic surgery, collaborating on anatomical variation, surgical planning and implant design.

 We are seeking a Research Fellow to undertake statistical shape modelling (SSM), CT-based three-dimensional analysis and patient-specific planning for complex hip reconstruction, covering acetabular and femoral approaches.

 You will demonstrate scientific writing through doctoral research and publications or conference submissions, and develop, validate and document reproducible computational or image-analysis workflows, with a commitment to research integrity and responsible data management.

 You will be proficient in medical-image processing, three-dimensional CAD or related software, with effective organisation, communication and collaboration skills. Experience in FEA, additive-manufacturing metrology or custom orthopaedic implant assessment would be advantageous.

Job Title: Research Fellow

Reference:  619             

Department: Mathematics

Contract Type: Fixed-term contract

Fixed Term End Date: 30 September 2029

Hours: Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date: Thursday 17 December 2026, 11:59pm (UK)                      

Full time Salary Range: £37,369 - £46,970 per annum

About the Role

Two-Year Fixed Term Contract starting October 2027 or earlier.

 

Applications are invited to work with Prof. Felix Schulze and collaborators on the ERC Project “GENREG – Generic regularity of area minimising hypersurfaces and mean curvature flows” at the University of Warwick.

 

The work is situated in Geometric Analysis, drawing on the interplay between PDE Theory, Geometric Flows, Riemannian Geometry and Geometric Measure Theory. The questions to be addressed revolve around the idea of generic regularity for either minimal surfaces or geometric flows. While it is not necessary that you have expertise in all these areas, it is expected that you are interested and willing to learn the background of the other areas necessary for project. 

 

You will be working as part of an inclusive and flexible team, based in the Warwick Maths Institute, a world-leading mathematics department. You will have, if desired, opportunities to travel in the UK and abroad, on research visits to collaborating groups and to conferences. You will be given both time and mentoring support to develop your own research profile and broader skills. 

 

Informal enquiries to be sent to Prof. Felix Schulze - felix.schulze@warwick.ac.uk

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here) 

About You

You should have (or be due to submit soon) a PhD, or have equivalent experience, in Geometric Analysis (preferably in Nonlinear PDE Theory, the Calculus of Variations, Geometric Flows, Riemannian Geometry or Geometric Measure Theory).

 

You can work effectively in a larger research group and have the ability to communicate its results to the wider research community.

 

You will have excellent communication and presentation skills, and be comfortable talking about your work with academics from other disciplines and non-specialists. You will have a record of research papers published in journals (or accepted to be published). You will have a high capacity for original research and creative thought, as well as the ability to manage your time effectively across multiple strands of research. 

 

You will be working as part of an inclusive and flexible team, based in the Warwick Maths Institute, a world-leading mathematics department. You will have, if desired, opportunities to travel in the UK and abroad, on research visits to collaborating groups and to conferences. You will be given both time and mentoring support to develop your own research profile and broader skills.

 

This position is suitable for a finishing PhD student, provided you will have submitted your thesis before the start of this position.  If you have not yet been awarded your PhD but are near submission or have recently submitted your PhD, any offers of employment will be made as Research Assistant on level 5 of the University grade structure. Upon successful award of your PhD and evidence of this fact, you will be promoted to Research Fellow on the first point of level 6 of the University grade structure.

About the Department

The Warwick Mathematics Institute is internationally recognised for its research and our best undergraduates are a match for those at any other UK university. We run a wide range of weekly seminar series, and many workshops and conferences, for which our Mathematics Research Centre provides organisational support.

 

A list of our staff and their research interests can be found at https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/maths/research/researchers

 

and you can see our undergraduate module pages at https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/maths/currentstudents/ughandbook

 

We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment, and we would particularly welcome applications from groups that are under-represented in UK mathematics. We are working hard towards improving our gender balance: we currently hold a Bronze Athena Swan award and our energetic Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion committee plays a significant role in shaping departmental policy.

 

We are an internationally diverse department. For those eligible, the University offers relocation and Immigration Support Scheme packages to assist with costs of relocating and any associated visa applications and IHS (health) surcharge fees.

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter by the closing date stated. 

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications.

 

Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

The application should include the following documents: CV, a list of publications and a research statement. All applicants should ensure that their three referees are included within thier application.

 

Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria.   

 

The interviews will be held on the week commencing 18th January 2027.

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

We are seeking a curious and motivated postdoctoral researcher to investigate how viruses exploit host membrane proteases to promote viral replication and trigger infection-specific signalling pathways.

 

Our lab investigates the emerging non-canonical functions of the signal peptidase complex in membrane protein biogenesis, cellular signalling and gene regulation. This project offers an exciting opportunity to combine mechanistic cell biology, biochemistry and virology to uncover fundamental mechanisms of virus–host interactions.

 

We are keen to hear from independent and creative scientists with a strong research background in cell biology and/or molecular virology. Hands-on experience with membrane proteins or RNA viruses is advantageous but training is available in-house and through expert collaborators.

 

You will lead and shape your research under the mentorship of Dr Dulloo, within a growing team, and support the training of other group members, graduate and undergraduate students.

 

Our lab is committed to combining ambitious, high-impact science with an exceptional research culture. We are a non-hierarchical, and supportive team that values scientific rigour, openness, mutual respect, and kindness.

Any requests for further information about the role can be directed to iqbal.dulloo@warwick.ac.uk

A DPhil/PhD in cell biology, virology or a related field, with a strong record of independent research.

Applications are invited for a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Candidate to  join the Napier group in the School of Life Sciences at Warwick University.

 

The successful candidate will become part of the Horizon Europe-funded MSCA Doctoral Network (DN) AGRIPOLYS and will undertake doctoral research under the supervision of Professor Richard Napier.

 

This Research Training Network AGRIPOLYS will train young scholars in developing the design principles for fully biodegradable and functional polymers that provide controlled release of agrochemicals and treatment of plants and seeds. This post at Warwick Life Sciences will determine the structural characteristics for polymers that enhance RNA loading (and other plant protection agents), and controlled delivery into plants.

 

You will work with the polymer chemists to devise and make polymers suited to the delivery of plant protection agents, using fluorescence microscopy and other molecular monitoring techniques to record and diagnose efficacy in plants.

 

There will be 3-Months secondments to the University of Padua, Italy, to learn synthetic strategies to polymeric carriers for RNA delivery to plants and to Syngenta (UK) to learn about formulation, legislation and scaling from bench to factory, and to discuss priority targets for RNA-mediated pest control.

 

Further information is available at https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101311807/en

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

 These Doctoral Candidates positions are offered in conjunction with PhD studentships at the University of Warwick, subject to the applicants satisfying the University’s admissions requirements. We are looking for someone with expertise in plant biology and agrochemistry, especially those with experience in fluorescence (confocal) microscopy. We also welcome applications from people with experience in PCR and allied molecular techniques and an interest in applying advanced analytical techniques to plants. Applicants must have an interest in agriculture and need to be able to converse easily with synthetic chemists.
